Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 106, verses 1–2:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh,﴾ ﴿their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer.﴾ Quraysh are a tribe (ḥayy) of the Arabs of the Ḥijāz, who are descended from Ma'add ibn 'Adnān. However, one is only called Qurashī (Qurayshi) if he is of the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah. They are divided into clans (afkhādh) and houses (buyūt), such as Banū Hāshim, Banū Umayyah, Banū Makhzūm, and others. The tribe was named Quraysh only because of tagarrush (qarash), and al-tagarrush means earning a livelihood, and they were merchants. It is related from Mu'āwiyah that he asked Ibn 'Abbās, "Why was Quraysh named Quraysh?" He said, "After a creature in the sea that eats but is not eaten, and that overcomes but is not overcome." They lived in Makkah, and they had two journeys every year for trade: a journey in winter to Yemen and a journey in summer to Syria. It is also said: both journeys were to Syria. It is also said: they would travel in summer to al-Ṭā'if, where there is water and shade, and would stay there, and in winter they would travel to Makkah, as that was their dwelling. The word īlāf (accustomed security) is a verbal noun from your saying ālaftu al-makān, "I became accustomed to the place," when you grew accustomed to it. It is also said that it is transitive by the hamzah, from alifa, "the man became accustomed to the thing," and allafahu iyyāhu, "another made him accustomed to it." So the meaning according to the first view is that Quraysh became accustomed to the winter and summer journeys, and according to the second, that God made them accustomed to the two journeys. Scholars differed regarding the connection of His saying "for the accustomed security of Quraysh" in three views. The first: it is connected to His saying "let them worship," and the meaning is "let them worship the Lord of this House, because of their accustomed security in the two journeys, for that is a blessing from God upon them." The second: it is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being "be amazed at the accustomed security of Quraysh." The third: it is connected to the surah of the Elephant, and the meaning is that God destroyed the companions of the Elephant for the accustomed security of Quraysh; so it is connected to His saying ﴿so He made them﴾ [al-Fīl: 5] or to what precedes it of verbs. This is supported by the fact that the two surahs were one surah in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with no separation between them, and 'Umar recited them both in a single rak'ah of the Maghrib prayer. God mentioned the accustomed security in general, then substituted for it the accustomed security restricted to the two journeys, to magnify the matter. He put "journey" in the accusative because it is the object of "their accustomed security," and he said "journey" while meaning "two journeys," as in the saying of the poet:

"Eat of some of your bellies, so that you may be spared (from hunger)."

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 106, verse 3–4:

﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾. This is a means of establishing the proof against them, with gentleness, an invitation to them, and a reminder of blessings. The House is the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). ﴿Who has fed them against hunger﴾. It may mean that He fed them because of the two journeys (al-rihlatayn), for it is related that before that they were in severe hardship and straitened circumstances, to the point that they ate carrion. It may also mean that He fed them in general, for the people of Makkah were settled in a valley without cultivation, yet God fed them with what was brought to them from the lands, in answer to the supplication of their father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), which is His saying: ﴿And provide its people with fruits﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126]. ﴿And made them safe from fear﴾. It may mean: He made them safe from the fear of the People of the Elephant. It may also mean: He made them safe in their own land, in answer to Ibrahim's supplication in His saying: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126], and we have explained this in its place. Or it means: He made them safe in their travels, for in their journeys they were secure, and no one would harm them, whereas other people had their wealth and their lives taken. It has been said: He made them safe from leprosy, so that no leper is seen in Makkah. Al-Zamakhshari said: the indefiniteness in "hunger" and "fear" is for their intensity.
